step: ADR 0003 section 9 step 27, R1 (issue #47): seconds and joules per accepted change, R1 raw block store (file-backed O_DIRECT) beside A2 on ext4, against the flush bound. Rerun at 222c24d after review of PR #103 (rotation flushes zero, header, commit separately; bench creates its own device file).
host: spark-b87b, 20 CPUs, kernel 7.0.0-1019-nvidia; both arms on /dev/nvme0n1p2 ext4: A2 as files in a directory, R1 on a 512 MiB regular file the bench creates per cell (O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, written with zeros, synced), opened by the store with O_DIRECT, formatted, removed after the cell
commands: 3 x interleaved: synapse-bench segments --dir <dir> --out raw-r1-<i>.json --reps 1 --block-device <path that does not exist>; synapse-bench segments --dir <dir> --out raw-a2-<i>.json --reps 1   (defaults otherwise: --agents 1,4,8,32 --changes 4000 --blob-bytes 11949 --segment-mib 16 --checkpoint-every 1000 --idle-window-s 30 --block-device-mib 512 --block-meta-mib 64)
aggregate.sh > summary.json   (median and range of the three invocations per arm and agent count)
energy: aien_spbm hwmon, SoC package only, 1 mJ step, 10 Hz sampling, uncalibrated; NVMe UNMEASURED. Idle window per invocation read 22.6 to 34.4 W.
note: Shared host, lighter load than the 57d1135 run (load average 2.4 vs 6 to 8.5) and a lower flush floor (0.802 ms vs 0.894 ms), so the two sessions are not directly comparable; the interleaved R1/A2 comparison inside this session is the measurement.
